Elite|OTE]] Second Team (2023) }} '''Tyler Smith''' (born November 2, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. ==Early life and high school career== Smith was born in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]] and relocated with his family to [[Houston, Texas]] after they were was displaced by [[Hurricane Katrina]] in 2005.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Crain|title=Walking Mismatch: G League Ignite's Tyler Smith Blends Fluidity with Size|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/g-league-ignite-tyler-smith-fluidity-size-story-background-nba-draft|website=[[SI.com]]|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023}} Smith attended [[George Bush High School]].{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Young|title=Bush's Tyler Smith leaving school to sign with Overtime Elite|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/highschool/article/Bush-Tyler-Smith-Bryce-Griggs-Overtime-Elite-OTE-16405358.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=August 23, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2023}} Smith was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Zucker|title=5-Star PF Tyler Smith Skips College, Signs '7-Figure' Overtime Elite Contract|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10010869-5-star-pf-tyler-smith-skips-college-signs-7-figure-overtime-elite-contract|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=August 22, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2023}} He had scholarship offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], among others.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Young|title=How Bryce Griggs, Tyler Smith are doing at Overtime Elite|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/hs-sports/article/Bryce-Griggs-Tyler-Smith-OTE-Overtime-Elite-pro-17674056.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=December 26, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Overtime Elite (2021–2023)=== Smith opted not to pursue a collegiate career and signed a two-year contract with [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE), a new professional league based in Atlanta with players between ages 16 and 20, on August 22, 2021.{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=Tyler Smith, No. 8 basketball prospect in 2023 class, signs with Overtime Elite|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32069127/tyler-smith-no-8-basketball-prospect-2023-class-signs-elite|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=August 22, 2021|access-date=November 14, 2023}} In his second season, he played for team Cold Hearts and was named second team All-OTE after averaging 15.7 points, eight rebounds, 1.9 steals, and 1.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Tipton|title=Overtime Elite's Tyler Smith signs with G-League Ignite|url=https://www.on3.com/news/overtime-elite-tyler-smith-signs-with-g-league-ignite/|website=On3.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2023}} ===NBA G League Ignite (2023–2024)=== Smith signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]] on June 30, 2023.{{cite press release|title=Tyler Smith & Izan Almansa Sign With Ignite|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/tyler-smith-izan-almansa-sign-with-ignite|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External
